title: Finland Detects a Strike on a Russian Warship in the Baltic Sea, Washington Demands Japan Triple Troop Hosting Payments to $19B, and the US Navy Outlines Its SSN(X) Drone Mothership
subhead: Finnish forces detect a strike on a Russian warship in the Baltic as Ukraine reports fresh Starshield satellite disruptions; Trump demands Tokyo pay $19 billion over five years to host US forces; the US Navy details its SSN(X) attack submarine after relieving the USS South Dakota command triad; and a Turkish S-70 helicopter crash kills four soldiers.

sections.heading: Finland Detects Strike on Russian Warship in Baltic Sea as Starshield Disruptions Return
sections.body:
Finland's armed forces disclosed on Thursday that they detected a strike against a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea on Wednesday, Defense News and Al Jazeera reported, while noting that the broader maritime security posture in the Baltic remains stable. On the eastern front, Ukrainian officials told Defense News, The War Zone, and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte that US-supplied Starshield military satellite terminals suffered their second bandwidth disruption in a month just as US envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin—though SpaceX denied altering the service.

Meanwhile, Ukraine's Permanent Representative to NATO, Alyona Getmanchuk, announced that two Ukrainian defense technology companies won NATO procurement tenders for the first time, M5 Dergi reported, while Poland and Germany contracted Polish AI firm SATIM to automate synthetic aperture radar (SAR) military satellite imagery analysis.
sections.whyItMatters: A kinetic strike on a Russian naval vessel in the Baltic Sea and recurring Starshield satellite degradations in Ukraine highlight how contested maritime and orbital communications domains remain during peace talks.

sections.heading: Washington Demands Japan Triple Troop Hosting Payments to $19B as Pentagon Greenlights Poland Base
sections.body:
The Trump administration has demanded that Japan triple its financial contribution for hosting US military forces to more than 3 trillion yen ($19 billion) over five years starting in fiscal 2027, the South China Morning Post reported citing diplomatic sources. In Australia, former Foreign Minister Bob Carr told The Guardian that the $368 billion AUKUS pact is "living a lie" and that Canberra will never receive US Virginia-class nuclear submarines—even as US Undersecretary of Defense for Policy Elbridge Colby and Navy officials told Breaking Defense that AUKUS Pillar I rotational deployments remain on or ahead of schedule with the USS Colorado.

In Europe, Polish Defense Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz announced that the Pentagon has officially "greenlit" a permanent US troop presence in Poland, leaving final approval to the White House in early December, Defense News reported. Elsewhere in the alliance, Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama stated that the 2027 NATO summit will no longer be held in Tirana amid domestic protests and criticism over defense spending, Al Jazeera noted.
sections.whyItMatters: Demanding a threefold burden-sharing hike from Tokyo while approving a permanent garrison in Warsaw shows Washington simultaneously squeezing Indo-Pacific allies on host-nation support and shifting its European footprint eastward.

sections.heading: US Navy Details SSN(X) Undersea Drone Mothership After Relieving USS South Dakota Command Triad
sections.body:
The US Navy is finalizing the analysis of alternatives for its next-generation SSN(X) nuclear attack submarine, designing the boat to be faster, easier to maintain, and capable of serving as a "lethal mothership" for a constellation of autonomous undersea drones, the service's submarine requirements chief told USNI News. Simultaneously, Vice Admiral Rob Gaucher told Breaking Defense that delivering the first Columbia-class ballistic missile submarine in 2028 remains "absolutely achievable" despite industrial bottlenecks.

The modernization push comes amid operational accountability actions across the fleet: USNI News reported that the Navy relieved the entire command triad—commanding officer, executive officer, and chief of the boat—of the Virginia-class attack submarine USS South Dakota (SSN-790) on October 14 following an undisclosed grounding incident, and quietly removed Commander Caitlin Cunningham as commanding officer of the destroyer USS Michael Murphy in September. In the Indo-Pacific, the US transferred two T38 Devil Ray unmanned surface vessels to the Philippine Marine Corps at Subic Bay, while the UK Royal Navy announced carrier trials for Northrop Grumman's Talon IQ autonomous aircraft demonstrator in 2027.
sections.whyItMatters: Relieving the command triad of an advanced Block III Virginia-class submarine after a grounding underscores the operational strain on the US undersea fleet even as it plans the SSN(X) successor.

sections.heading: US Indicts Three in Iranian-Backed Plot on RAF Fairford as Congressional Democrats Target Israel Tech Clause
sections.body:
US federal prosecutors indicted three men—one operating from inside a prison—for allegedly conspiring on behalf of Iran-aligned networks to carry out roughly 20 terrorist attacks across the United States and Europe, including a plot targeting RAF Fairford, the British base used by US strategic bombers, Defense News reported. In the Middle East, Al Jazeera noted that Iranian forces targeted a US radar facility in Bahrain while Saudi-led coalition defenses intercepted a wave of Houthi drones after the UN Security Council extended sanctions.

In Washington, House Democrats launched an effort to strip a US-Israel weapons technology cooperation measure from the annual defense authorization bill, Defense News reported, while the House passed legislation allowing combat-injured veterans with fewer than 20 years of service to collect full retirement and disability pay. Inside the Pentagon, Breaking Defense reported that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is moving to elevate the top civilian overseeing Special Operations Forces (SOF) to service-secretary status, and Forbes noted Hegseth awarded the Army sentinel who reprimanded his delegation for noise at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier.
sections.whyItMatters: The indictment over an Iranian-backed plot against RAF Fairford explains this week's sudden evacuation of US Air Force tankers from British bases.

sections.heading: Turkish S-70 Helicopter Crash Kills Four Soldiers as ASELSAN Displays KORAL-2 Electronic Warfare System
sections.body:
A Turkish Land Forces Sikorsky S-70 Black Hawk utility helicopter crashed in the Yeşilyurt district of Malatya on Thursday evening, killing four military personnel—two pilot majors and two technical non-commissioned officers—Turkey's Ministry of National Defense announced via SavunmaSanayiST and Tolga Özbek. Meanwhile, during a visit by Gendarmerie Commander General Ali Çardakçı to ASELSAN's campus, imagery emerged of the new KORAL-2 next-generation land-based electronic warfare and attack system ahead of its entry into inventory alongside SİPER, HİSAR, and KORKUT air defense batteries.

In defense industrial diplomacy, 69 Turkish and 30 Saudi defense companies held 601 bilateral business meetings during the two-day Turkey-Saudi Arabia Defense Industry Days in Istanbul focused on joint production, Independent Türkçe reported. Elsewhere, France, Sweden, and the Greek Cypriot Administration signed a framework deal to jointly procure MBDA's Akeron MP anti-tank missiles using the EU's SAFE financing mechanism, Portugal allocated €82.35 million to modernize its Leopard 2A6 tanks, Taiwan received its fifth F-16 Block 70 fighter, and high-speed aircraft startup Hermeus partnered with Northrop Grumman on hypersonic drones, M5 Dergi and The War Zone reported.
sections.whyItMatters: KORAL-2's imminent induction expands Turkey's stand-off radar jamming reach, while 601 Turkish-Saudi industrial meetings point toward co-production deals in the Gulf.

bottomLine: A kinetic strike on a Russian warship in the Baltic Sea and an indictment uncovering an Iranian-backed plot against RAF Fairford highlight escalating hybrid threats in Europe, while Washington demands $19 billion in troop-hosting payments from Japan and greenlights a permanent garrison in Poland.
sources: Defense News, Al Jazeera, The War Zone, M5 Dergi, South China Morning Post, The Guardian, Breaking Defense, USNI News, Forbes, SavunmaSanayiST, Tolga Özbek, Independent Türkçe
